title: Autoscaler sensitivity regression: HPA/KEDA misfires causing capacity oscillation
creator: Asha Menon
summary: A regression in autoscaler sensitivity caused repeated KEDA-triggered scale-ups and HPA scale-downs for the realtime-inference service. The oscillation increased p99 latency and resulted in elevated tail errors for 45 minutes during business hours. This doc captures timeline, root cause, mitigations, and action items to prevent recurrence.
impact: ~45 minutes of elevated p99 latency for realtime-inference (peak 850ms vs baseline 120ms). Error rate for downstream request paths increased from 0.3% to 2.7%. No customer data was lost; several customers reported degraded response times to support.
timeline: 2026-03-09 09:12 UTC - Alert: realtime-inference p99 > 700ms; on-call paged
2026-03-09 09:18 UTC - Triage: observed rapid pod churn for inference-worker; KEDA scale events spike followed by HPA rapid scale-downs
2026-03-09 09:25 UTC - Rapid mitigation: Increased minReplicas to keep warm capacity; mitigation reduced latency but did not eliminate thrash
2026-03-09 09:40 UTC - Root cause hypothesis: new metric exporter change deployed earlier that day removed 60s smoothing window, exposing transient queue spikes to KEDA
2026-03-09 10:05 UTC - Temporary rollback: Reverted metric exporter change; KEDA behavior returned to expected range and system stabilized by 10:20 UTC
2026-03-09 10:30 UTC - Incident declared resolved; post-incident follow-ups assigned
root_cause: A configuration change to the Redis queue metric exporter (PR #1876) removed a moving-average smoothing step to 'improve freshness'. This exposed short-lived queue spikes (~10-30s) to KEDA, which triggered scale-up events. HPA was configured to aggressively scale down based on CPU with a short stabilization window, producing a feedback loop: KEDA scale-ups followed by rapid HPA scale-downs, causing pod churn and increased cold-start latency.
contributing_factors: Metric exporter change removed smoothing that filtered transient bursts
KEDA was using un-smoothed queue depth with a short polling interval (5s)
HPA downscale stabilization was too aggressive (30s) and used CPU which lags compared to queue metrics
No canary rollout of metrics change; change deployed to all regions simultaneously
Warm pool size for realtime-inference was minimal; pod startup cold-start penalty is ~600ms per replica
Runbook lacked a specific section mapping KEDA/HPA interactions for queue-based autoscaling
mitigations_taken: Rolled back metric exporter PR #1876 to restore 60s smoothing
Increased minReplicas from 2 to 4 during incident window to maintain warm capacity
Adjusted KEDA polling interval from 5s to 15s as a temporary band-aid
Updated alert thresholds to surface pod churn (scale events per minute) earlier
permanent_fixes_and_decisions: Restore smoothing by default in the metric exporter and make the smoothing window configurable; default=60s
Introduce percentile-based HPA metric for CPU (p95) instead of average to better reflect tail pressure
Adjust HPA downscale stabilization to 3 minutes and add cooldown to avoid immediate downscales after KEDA scale-ups
Add a small warm pool (reserved replicas) for realtime-inference with gradual autoscale bypass for the pool
Change KEDA polling interval default for queue-backed scalers to 15s and add jitter to avoid synchronized triggers
Require canary rollout (10% traffic for 30m with automatic rollback) for metric/telemetry changes

ENG-93423: Change HPA downscale stabilization to 180s for queue-backed services and roll out via canary (owner: Diego Ramirez) - due 2026-03-21
ENG-93424: Implement percentile CPU metric in metrics pipeline and update HPA config (owner: Marcus Li) - due 2026-03-28
ENG-93425: Create warm pool operator task to reserve idle replicas for critical realtime services (owner: Elena Kuznetsova) - due 2026-04-04
ENG-93426: Update runbook with KEDA/HPA interaction section and playbook for scale-thrash incidents (owner: Asha Menon) - due 2026-03-16
ENG-93427: Add automated test to chaos harness simulating short queue bursts to validate autoscaler behavior (owner: Nate O'Connor) - due 2026-04-01
telemetry_changes: Add dashboard: autoscaler/thrash-events (counts of KEDA scale events and HPA scale events per minute)
Add SLO guardrail: alert if >6 scale events per 10m for a service
Instrument metric exporter to emit smoothing_version tag and rollout id for easier debugging
retrospective_notes: We underestimated coupling between queue-level scalers (KEDA) and resource-based autoscalers (HPA). Small telemetry changes can have outsized operational effects when different controllers act on different signals with incompatible stabilization windows. The team will treat telemetry changes with the same caution as control-plane changes (canary + automatic validation).
